title: Patterns
examples: Teacher, what shape comes next in this line?
Can you show me a pattern with three different shapes?

explain.say: Look at these shapes. Red, blue, red, blue. Say the colors with me.
We see a pattern here. It repeats red and then blue. This is an AB pattern.
Next, look at this one. Circle, square, square. Circle, square, square. This is an ABB pattern.
Now we have three different shapes. Triangle, circle, square. Triangle, circle, square. This is an ABC pattern.
If the pattern is red, green, blue. Red, green, blue. What color comes next? You must say the first color again.

faq.q: What does it mean to spot a pattern?
faq.a: It means you can see what is going to happen next. You look for things that repeat in an order. You might also ask, what is the rule here?
asks: How do I find the pattern?
What is the rule for this group?

faq.q: If the pattern is circle, square, circle, square, what comes next?
faq.a: The pattern is repeating circle and square. So the next shape must be a circle. You can also ask, what shape goes here?

faq.q: Can I use more than three shapes in a pattern?
faq.a: Yes, you can use many shapes. The pattern just needs to repeat in a clear order. You might also ask, does it have to be only three?
asks: What if I use four shapes?
Does the pattern have to be short?

faq.q: What if the pattern seems wrong?
faq.a: If it looks wrong, you need to check the rule. Look at the shapes before and after the mistake. You can also ask, where is the mistake?
asks: How do I fix this pattern?
Is this shape in the right place?

faq.q: Is 'AB' the same as 'A A B B'?
faq.a: No, they are different patterns. AB means one of A, then one of B. AABB means two of A, then two of B. You can also ask, are they the same?
asks: What is the difference between AB and AABB?
Can you show me two different patterns?

facts: Patterns are things that repeat in a regular order.
An AB pattern repeats two different things.
An ABC pattern repeats three different things.
You can find patterns in nature, like leaves or stripes.

quiz.why: The pattern is repeating circle and triangle. The next shape must be a circle.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you are adding too many shapes, but only one shape is needed to continue the pattern.
wrong.2: This is tempting because the last shape was a triangle, but the pattern must repeat the first shape.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it is a different shape, but the pattern must stick to the same shapes.

quiz.say: What is the pattern: Red, Blue, Blue, Red, Blue, Blue, ?
quiz.show: R, B, B, R, B, B, ?
quiz.why: The pattern is repeating red, blue, blue. The next shape must start the pattern over with red.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you are trying to show the whole next group, but only one shape is needed now.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it looks like a simple AB pattern, but the rule is actually ABB.
wrong.3: This is tempting because blue is the most common color here, but the pattern rule is red, blue, blue.

quiz.say: If the pattern is A, B, C, A, B, C, what shape should replace the question mark?
quiz.show: A, B, C, A, B, C, ?
quiz.why: The pattern is repeating A, B, and C in order. After C, the pattern starts again with A.

wrong.0: This is tempting because B comes after A, but the pattern rule is to go back to the start.
wrong.1: This is tempting because C was the last shape shown, but the pattern must restart.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you are predicting the next two shapes, but only one shape is needed to continue the sequence.
